blocks.text: Blue Owl Technology Finance Corp. | Coverage: BDCs / technology direct lending    |    Data to 4 Nov 2026 (share price to Oct 13)

Verdict: the Q3'26 print validated NAV and the dividend but delivered the first real credit datapoint — and our own P/NAV trigger line is breached. NAV rose for the first time since Q4'25 (+0.8% to $16.62, marks positive two straight quarters); the Q4'26 base was held at $0.35; non-accruals tripled to 1.8% of cost on the Signifyd preferred — still the lowest of the six peers on Q2'26 data, but no longer an order of magnitude below the industry. At $9.21 / 0.55x the stock trades through the 0.60x line set in Section 4 last quarter: per the framework, the position goes back to IC two-way rather than defaulting to hold.

items: Q3'26 results (11/4) and dividend decision (11/3): NAV $16.62, +0.8% QoQ, first rise since Q4'25; adjusted NII $0.29 vs the $0.32 Earnings Whispers consensus — a miss; non-accruals 1.8% of cost; $55.2mm repurchased in Q3 at ~$11.03 average; the Q4'26 base dividend was held at $0.35 rather than cut toward NII.

Second lawsuit added (10/7): Girard Sharp filed a securities class action for former OTF II shareholders who received OTF stock in the March 24, 2025 merger, citing the share-price decline since issuance — alongside the 36(b) excessive-fee suit filed 6/18. Near-term economics limited; the discovery risk now runs on two tracks.
New 52-week low (10/13): $9.14 intraday in a global tech selloff, prior close $9.21; sell-side consensus Moderate Buy, average target $13.60, 4 Buy / 3 Hold — implying +48% vs the Oct 13 close.

Blue Owl redemption pressure rotated, not resolved: OTIC 3Q requests rose to 39% of shares, $1.1bn (2Q: 38.1%) while OCIC eased to 16.8% (2Q: 18.8%); $4.2bn combined, and the 5% cap bound for a third straight quarter. Contrast: KKR's K-FITS went past its 5% cap to pay all requests in full.

Macro and industry: the 10-year UST touched 5.35% intraday on Oct 7, the highest since 2002, and ended that week at 5.24%, +107bp YTD; gating reached Australia as Metrics Credit Partners (~A$40bn) froze redemptions on some funds after its auditor declined to sign off.

Left: OTF vs the BDC sector on non-accruals — the sector's five-year high is itself Medallia-driven, and OTF converges toward the mean from below. Right: share price since the June 2025 listing — OTF ~−44%, worst of the BDC set and the visual source of the 0.55x discount.

items: The transmission channel is still valuation first, but credit has entered: ~47.6% of fair value sits in the heaviest-migration end-markets (software 32.3% + healthcare tech 12.3% + healthcare providers 3.0%, Q3'26 10-Q). The Q1'26 −0.84 write-down was spread-driven and marks have run positive two straight quarters (+$0.03, +$0.19/sh); Q3'26 added the first credit-channel datapoint — the Signifyd preferred.

OTF's own data is now mixed: cohort EBITDA printed its first QoQ decline, $291mm → $287mm (deck p.7, one quarter in arrears), though EV rose to $6.2bn and Net LTV held 40%; PIK is down every reported quarter to 11.5%; non-accruals at fair value 1.1% vs the 2.87% industry cost average — still below, no longer an order of magnitude.

Three changes: net leverage rose a fifth straight quarter to 0.94x; base coverage slipped 86% → 83%, so the payout leans on spillover with specials ended; and the yield reset is in the price — at $9.21 the $0.35 base yields ~15.1%, so the income-rotation risk is largely realized, not pending.

blocks.html: 4. Our Position: Assessment, Watch List & Action
blocks.text: 4. Our Position: Assessment, Watch List & Action

items: Overall assessment: fundamentals validated ex-credit, valuation trigger breached — back to IC per our own framework. Credit remains lowest-of-six on non-accruals (1.8% vs TSLX 1.9% at Q2'26) but is no longer unambiguously clean; the discount is the deepest at 0.55x; consensus target $13.60 (+48% vs $9.21); the risks are application-software concentration (53.4% of fair value on the house T3 re-tier, pending freeze), the rating-3 build to 9.0%, and two lawsuits.

blocks.text: Action: re-table at IC. The 0.60x P/NAV trigger set last quarter is breached (0.55x on the Q3'26 NAV), and the discussion is two-way by design. The hold case: NAV +0.8%, base dividend held, marks positive two straight quarters, non-accruals still lowest of six on Q2'26 peer data, consensus +48% to target. The bear case gained its first datapoint: non-accruals 0.6% → 1.8% of cost and the rating-3 build to 9.0%. Our framing into IC: the discount prices the 2027–28 software-credit and platform thesis, not the reported book — position unchanged until IC rules.
